Arcane Resistance.description: At 2nd level, the hexblade gains a supernatural bonus on saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities equal to his Charisma bonus (with a minimum bonus of +1).

Aura of Unlucky.description: At 12th level, a hexblade can activate a supernatural aura of ill fortune once per day as a free action. While this aura is active, all melee and ranged attacks directed at the hexblade have a 20% miss chance (functioning like concealment). The aura persists for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the hexblade's Charisma bonus (minimum 3 rounds). At 16th level the hexblade can use this aura twice per day, and at 20th level it becomes usable three times per day.

Bonus Feat.description: At 5th level and every five levels after that (10th, 15th, and 20th), the hexblade receives a bonus feat chosen from the following options: Combat Casting, Greater Spell Focus (restricted to enchantment, necromancy, or transmutation), Greater Spell Penetration, Spell Focus (restricted to enchantment, necromancy, or transmutation), or Spell Penetration.

Dire Hexblade's Curse.description: At 19th level, the penalty imposed by the hexblade's curse on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls increases to -6 (up from -4).

Greater Hexblade's Curse.description: Upon reaching 7th level, the penalty inflicted by the hexblade's curse on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls increases to -4 (up from -2).

Hexblade's Curse.description: Once per day, a hexblade may place a curse on an enemy as a free action. The target must be visible and no farther than 60 feet away. A cursed creature suffers a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls, lasting 1 hour. A successful Will saving throw (DC 10 + half the hexblade's class level + the hexblade's Charisma modifier) prevents the effect entirely. Every four levels after 1st (at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level), the hexblade can use this ability one extra time per day. The penalties from multiple curses do not stack with each other, and a creature that resists the curse is immune to that hexblade's curse for 24 hours. Any spell or effect that lifts or dispels curses also ends this ability's effect.

Mettle.description: Beginning at 3rd level, the hexblade's resilience allows him to shrug off magical and supernatural attacks through sheer determination. When the hexblade succeeds on a Will or Fortitude saving throw against an effect that would normally deal reduced damage or impose a lesser effect on a successful save (such as a spell noted as Will half or Fortitude partial), the hexblade negates the effect entirely instead. A hexblade who is unconscious or asleep does not benefit from mettle.

Spells.description: Starting at 4th level, the hexblade gains access to a small repertoire of arcane spells drawn from the hexblade spell list. These spells are cast spontaneously without preparation, similar to how a sorcerer casts. A hexblade needs a Charisma score of at least 10 + the spell level to learn or cast a given spell (for example, Charisma 11 for 1st-level spells, Charisma 12 for 2nd-level spells, and so on). Saving throw DCs against hexblade spells equal 10 + the spell level + the hexblade's Charisma modifier. As with other spellcasting classes, the hexblade is limited to a set number of spells per day at each level, and a high Charisma score grants bonus daily spells. If a hexblade's base allotment for a given spell level is 0, only bonus spells from Charisma are available at that level. The hexblade's pool of known spells is very narrow; the hexblade starts knowing no spells and acquires new ones at specific levels. Charisma does not influence the total number of spells known. At 12th level and every third hexblade level thereafter (15th and 18th), the hexblade may exchange one known spell for a different spell of the same level, provided the spell being replaced is at least two levels lower than the highest-level hexblade spell available. For example, at 12th level the hexblade could swap a single 1st-level spell (since the maximum castable level is 3rd); at 15th level, a 1st- or 2nd-level spell could be traded (since 4th-level spells are now accessible). Only one spell may be swapped per level, and the decision must be made at the same time new spells known are gained. Through 3rd level, a hexblade possesses no caster level. Beginning at 4th level, the hexblade's caster level equals half the hexblade class level.

Summon Familiar.description: Starting at 4th level, the hexblade may acquire a familiar by spending 24 hours and 100 gp worth of magical materials. A familiar is a magical beast taking the form of a small creature that is tougher and more intelligent than a normal animal of its kind, serving as both companion and servant. The hexblade selects the type of familiar, and as the hexblade gains levels the familiar grows in power. For the purposes of determining the familiar's abilities and special powers, treat the hexblade as a sorcerer three levels lower. If the familiar is slain or dismissed, the hexblade must make a DC 15 Fortitude save; failure costs 200 experience points per hexblade level, while success halves that penalty. The hexblade's experience total cannot drop below 0 from this loss. A lost familiar cannot be replaced for a year and a day, though a slain familiar can be raised from the dead without losing a level or Constitution point. A character with multiple classes that grant familiars may only have one familiar at a time.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: A hexblade is proficient with all simple and martial weapons as well as light armor, but not shields. The somatic gestures for hexblade spells are straightforward enough that a hexblade can cast them while wearing light armor without risking arcane spell failure. Wearing medium or heavy armor, or carrying a shield, imposes the standard arcane spell failure chance on any hexblade spell that includes a somatic component (as most do). A hexblade who multiclasses still suffers normal arcane spell failure for spells gained from other arcane casting classes.

classFeatures.description: Hexblades are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with light armor but not with shields. Because the somatic components required for hexblade spells are simple, a hexblade can cast hexblade spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. However, like any other arcane spellcaster, a hexblade wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component (and most do). A multiclass hexblade still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells derived from other classes.

In effect, the hexblade "loses" the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell's level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least two levels lower than the highest-level hexblade spell the hexblade can cast. For instance, upon reaching 12th level, a hexblade could trade in a single 1st level spell (two spell levels below the highest-level hexblade spell he can cast, which is 3rd) for a different 1st-level spell.
